final_label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common transition) late in the episode (trial >= 88)

with_model_outputs.label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common) late in the episode (trial >= ~88)
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D2 steps where the agent chose a2 and reached S2 by the common transition (100% of mass; never on a1, S1, or rare a2->S1 or a1->S2), and only near the end of the episode: no activity before trial ~78, 5.5% of mass at trials 80-89, 94.5% at trials 90-99. Magnitude grows with episode trial index; activations rise steadily across consecutive a2->S2 trials in the same window, and the low-activation quartile sits at trials 85-89. That is why the ep_trial>=88 cutoff misses mostly weak activations (dev mass recall 0.98). The feature also lines up with low value-head output (96% of mass in the lowest value bin), which is consistent with the end-of-episode position. It does not fire at D1 or GO, and it ignores reward and the hidden good state beyond the a2/S2 bias. All variables are observed at D2, so no future variables are used. Dev: P 0.94, R 0.91, F1 0.92.

issues: All the categorical claims hold on the dev profile. 100% of activation mass is at D2, with in_action=2, state=2 and common=1. There is zero activity at D1, GO, on a1, on S1 or on rare transitions. Mass by trial: 0 before trial 70, 4 steps in trials 70-79, 5.5% in 80-89, 94.5% in 90-99. 96.4% of mass sits in the lowest value bin. Reward and prev_reward splits do not separate it: P stays at 0.92-0.97 within each, and recall splits roughly by base rate.

Reported scores reproduce. Test: P 0.922, R 0.921, F1 0.921, mass recall 0.985. Cutoff sweep on test: >=86 F1 0.896, >=87 0.915, >=88 0.921, >=89 0.913. The ep_trial>=88 edge is a soft threshold. Remaining misses (1.5% of mass on test) and false positives are weak activations (rel. act < ~0.3) around trials 85-89 on a2->S2c steps. They are not a separate phase, choice, transition or reward class.

Minor overclaim: magnitude is not simply 'growing with trial index'. Several of the top activating windows are a2->S2c steps right after a run of a1 choices (switch trials, stay==0). Those are a small share of mass (predicate with stay==0: P 0.99, R 0.07), but the strongest single activations are not only at the end of long a2 streaks.

Better boundary: swapping the trial cutoff for the model's own value output, (phase == D2) & (action == 2) & (state == 2) & (value < 5.6), gives test P 0.984, R 0.924, F1 0.953, mass recall 0.988. False positives drop from 1534 to 287. So the 'late in episode' condition is better read as 'low predicted value / few trials remaining', which is a smooth function of ep_trial. The value head may be partly downstream of this feature, so this is a refinement, not a refutation.

label: D2 after a2 -> S2 (common transition) late in the episode (trial >= 88)
explanation: Fires only at D2 when the agent chose a2 and landed in S2 (common transition), and only in the last ~12 trials of the episode (none before trial 78; rate 3% in trials 80-89, 14% in 90-99). Episode trial replaces the banned value output (value falls with episode time). Missed activations are weak (1.6% of activation mass) near the trial-88 boundary; the onset is soft between trials ~85 and ~90. Adding belief or previous action did not help.

issues: Claims check out on test: D2-only, common-only (a1->S2 rare at trial>=88 precision 0.0; a2->S1 precision 0.0001), zero activity before trial 78 (precision 0.0 on 307k D2 steps).

Remaining misses/FPs are weak activations around the soft trial ~85-90 onset (misses hold 1.5% mass); thresholds 86/90 give F1 0.896/0.886 vs 0.921 at 88. Belief and prev_action terms lower F1 (0.81, 0.79). No systematic counterexample class.
